definitionEn: Intended to teach, especially in an overly moralising or rigid teacher-led manner.
meaningVi: mang tính giáo huấn, thuyết giảng một chiều
existingExample: Modern universities are gradually moving away from purely didactic lectures toward collaborative problem-solving workshops.

definitionEn: A self-taught person who acquires advanced knowledge or skills without formal schooling.
meaningVi: người tự học không qua đào tạo chính quy
existingExample: With open-access repositories proliferating online, a disciplined autodidact can now master complex disciplines independently.

definitionEn: Relating to schools, academic study, and formal intellectual achievement.
meaningVi: thuộc về học thuật, trường lớp
existingExample: Excessive emphasis on scholastic rankings often pressures secondary schools into narrowing their arts programmes.

definitionEn: Having or showing deep, extensive knowledge gained through serious study and reading.
meaningVi: uyên bác, thông thái sâu rộng
existingExample: The keynote speaker delivered an erudite critique of how standardised testing narrows intellectual exploration.

definitionEn: To be formally admitted to study at a university or college after meeting entrance criteria.
meaningVi: chính thức nhập học vào trường đại học
existingExample: Targeted outreach initiatives have enabled far more first-generation students to matriculate at prestigious institutions.

definitionEn: Complementing and directly reinforcing the formal academic curriculum rather than remaining separate from it.
meaningVi: thuộc hoạt động bổ trợ gắn liền với chương trình học
existingExample: Debating societies and laboratory clubs offer valuable co-curricular experiences that sharpen analytical reasoning.

definitionEn: Designed to help students who are struggling to reach the expected academic standard.
meaningVi: bổ trợ, phụ đạo để khắc phục lỗ hổng kiến thức
existingExample: Early diagnostic screening allows schools to provide targeted remedial support before minor literacy gaps widen.

definitionEn: Ongoing evaluation during a course used to monitor comprehension and adapt teaching methods accordingly.
meaningVi: đánh giá quá trình trong học tập
existingExample: Unlike high-stakes final examinations, formative assessment gives teachers timely insight into conceptual misunderstandings.

definitionEn: Formal evaluation conducted at the end of an instructional period to measure overall mastery against benchmarks.
meaningVi: đánh giá tổng kết cuối kỳ hoặc cuối khóa
existingExample: Critics argue that relying exclusively on summative assessment encourages cramming rather than durable understanding.

definitionEn: The high standard of thoroughness, intellectual challenge, and precision expected in scholarly work.
meaningVi: tính chặt chẽ và chuẩn mực nghiêm ngặt trong học thuật
existingExample: Expanding university access must not come at the expense of maintaining academic rigour across degree programmes.

definitionEn: Awareness and deliberate regulation of one's own thinking and learning processes.
existingExample: Teaching adolescents strategies for metacognition significantly improves their ability to plan essays and self-correct errors.

definitionEn: Temporary instructional support provided by educators and gradually withdrawn as learners gain independence.
existingExample: Effective scaffolding enables novice writers to construct coherent arguments before tackling complex essays unassisted.

definitionEn: A teaching framework that tailors content, pacing, and tasks to accommodate diverse student abilities.
meaningVi: giảng dạy phân hóa theo năng lực từng học sinh
existingExample: In overcrowded classrooms, implementing differentiated instruction remains logistically demanding even for seasoned educators.

definitionEn: The process of acquiring knowledge and insight through direct practical involvement and structured reflection.
meaningVi: học tập qua trải nghiệm thực tế
existingExample: Fieldwork and industry placements exemplify experiential learning by bridging abstract theory with real-world complexity.

definitionEn: An educational approach in which students actively support and instruct one another to deepen mutual comprehension.
meaningVi: học tập tương trợ cùng bạn đồng trang lứa
existingExample: Universities increasingly embed peer-assisted learning into first-year modules to reduce attrition and boost confidence.

definitionEn: An individual possessing profound expertise across multiple distinct fields of knowledge.
meaningVi: nhà bác học tinh thông nhiều lĩnh vực
existingExample: Hyper-specialised degree tracks rarely cultivate the breadth of perspective associated with a classical polymath.

definitionEn: A young person endowed with exceptional talent or intellect far beyond their age.
meaningVi: thần đồng, người có tài năng xuất chúng từ sớm
existingExample: Accelerating a mathematical prodigy into university lectures without emotional support can inadvertently cause social alienation.

definitionEn: The highest-ranking graduating student selected to deliver the farewell address at commencement.
meaningVi: thủ khoa tốt nghiệp đại diện phát biểu
existingExample: Although she graduated as class valedictorian, she stressed that collaborative curiosity mattered more than grades.

definitionEn: A period of paid leave granted periodically to university academics for research, writing, or travel.
meaningVi: kỳ nghỉ phép nghiên cứu của giảng viên đại học
existingExample: During her year-long sabbatical, the professor compiled comparative datasets on bilingual primary schools across Europe.

definitionEn: Permanent academic employment status designed to safeguard scholars' freedom of inquiry and speech.
meaningVi: chế độ biên chế học thuật lâu dài cho giảng viên
existingExample: Defenders of university tenure contend that job security empowers researchers to pursue unconventional yet vital inquiries.

definitionEn: Financial assets donated to an educational institution to generate ongoing income for scholarships and research.
meaningVi: quỹ hiến tặng lâu dài cho cơ sở giáo dục
existingExample: Elite institutions with multibillion-dollar endowment funds can weather public funding cuts far better than regional colleges.

definitionEn: A monetary grant awarded to a student on the basis of financial need to help cover study costs.
meaningVi: học bổng hỗ trợ tài chính theo hoàn cảnh
existingExample: Without a means-tested bursary, many talented applicants from rural districts would be deterred by living expenses.

definitionEn: A fixed regular allowance paid to postgraduate researchers or fellows to cover basic living expenses.
meaningVi: khoản trợ cấp sinh hoạt định kỳ cho nghiên cứu sinh
existingExample: Unless doctoral stipend levels keep pace with urban rents, academia risks losing promising scholars to corporate jobs.

definitionEn: The university, college, or school that a person previously attended and graduated from.
meaningVi: trường cũ nơi từng theo học và tốt nghiệp
existingExample: Successful alumni frequently endow laboratories at their alma mater to expand research opportunities for younger cohorts.

definitionEn: An academic seminar or formal gathering where specialists present and debate recent research findings.
meaningVi: buổi tọa đàm, hội thảo học thuật chuyên sâu
existingExample: Weekly departmental colloquium sessions expose postgraduate students to rigorous questioning from visiting academics.

definitionEn: A formal conference at which multiple experts deliver papers and exchange views on a defined subject.
meaningVi: hội nghị chuyên đề quy tụ các chuyên gia
existingExample: An international education symposium in Helsinki examined how teacher autonomy correlates with student well-being.

definitionEn: A detailed, book-length scholarly study devoted to a single specialised subject.
meaningVi: chuyên khảo học thuật sâu về một chủ đề duy nhất
existingExample: Her landmark monograph on early literacy reform reshaped teacher-training curricula across three provinces.

definitionEn: A concise yet comprehensive collection of detailed information on a particular academic subject.
meaningVi: tuyển tập tóm lược toàn diện kiến thức
existingExample: The ministry published a digital compendium of evidence-based classroom interventions for secondary educators.

definitionEn: A structured pattern, acronym, or association used to assist in retaining and recalling information.
meaningVi: kỹ thuật hoặc công cụ hỗ trợ ghi nhớ
existingExample: While a clever mnemonic helps medical students recall anatomical sequences, conceptual mastery still requires clinical practice.

definitionEn: The total amount of mental effort being exerted in working memory during a learning task.
meaningVi: tải trọng nhận thức lên trí nhớ làm việc
existingExample: Cluttered multimedia slides increase extraneous cognitive load and hinder students from absorbing core concepts.

definitionEn: Higher-order mental skills including planning, impulse control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility.
meaningVi: chức năng điều hành nhận thức
existingExample: Early playful interaction strengthens executive functioning, which predicts long-term academic resilience better than memorisation.

definitionEn: An educational philosophy encouraging learners to question power structures, assumptions, and social inequities.
existingExample: Advocates of critical pedagogy contend that schooling should cultivate active citizens rather than passive test-takers.

definitionEn: Natural inclination or suitability for acquiring specific practical or technical occupational skills.
meaningVi: năng khiếu hướng nghiệp, khả năng bẩm sinh về nghề nghiệp
existingExample: Guidance counsellors should evaluate vocational aptitude alongside exam scores so students can pursue fulfilling trades.

definitionEn: Excessive reliance on formal academic degrees or certificates as the primary measure of competence.
meaningVi: chủ nghĩa sùng bái bằng cấp
existingExample: Growing credentialism has forced entry-level applicants to acquire master's degrees for roles that previously required on-the-job training.

definitionEn: An intrinsic desire to investigate complex ideas, ask probing questions, and pursue deeper understanding.
meaningVi: tinh thần ham hiểu biết và khám phá tri thức
existingExample: Rigidly scripted syllabuses often extinguish intellectual curiosity before pupils even reach upper secondary school.

definitionEn: Relating to knowledge, its sources, validity, and the degree of justification behind beliefs.
meaningVi: thuộc về tri thức luận và bản chất của sự hiểu biết
existingExample: University writing courses should foster epistemic humility so students evaluate competing evidence without dogmatism.

definitionEn: To instil an attitude, ethical principle, or intellectual habit firmly through persistent instruction.
existingExample: Primary schools play a pivotal role in helping to inculcate civic empathy and disciplined study habits early in life.

definitionEn: To instruct or enlighten someone in a way that improves their intellectual or moral understanding.
meaningVi: khai sáng, nâng cao trí tuệ và phẩm hạnh
existingExample: Publicly funded educational documentaries aim to edify broad audiences rather than merely chase commercial ratings.

definitionEn: To teach a person or group to accept a set of beliefs uncritically without tolerating dissent.
meaningVi: nhồi sọ, áp đặt tư tưởng một chiều không cho phản biện
existingExample: Democratic curricula are explicitly designed to educate citizens in critical inquiry rather than indoctrinate them with dogma.

definitionEn: A formal warning period during which a student whose grades fall below minimum standards must improve to remain enrolled.
meaningVi: tình trạng cảnh cáo học vụ
existingExample: Universities that pair academic probation with structured mentoring report markedly higher retention rates.

definitionEn: the cutting down of large areas of forest.
existingExample: Large-scale deforestation threatens countless plant and animal species.

definitionEn: the amount of carbon dioxide produced by the activities of a person or organisation.
meaningVi: dấu chân carbon (lượng khí thải CO₂)
existingExample: Cycling to work is a simple way to reduce your carbon footprint.

definitionEn: energy from sources that are naturally replaced, such as wind or sunlight.
existingExample: Governments should offer subsidies to households that switch to renewable energy.

definitionEn: fuels such as coal, oil and gas formed from the remains of ancient organisms.
existingExample: Burning fossil fuels is the main cause of rising greenhouse gas levels.

definitionEn: the variety of plants and animals in a particular place.
existingExample: Coral reefs support an extraordinary level of biodiversity.

definitionEn: a type of animal or plant that may soon disappear completely.
meaningVi: loài có nguy cơ tuyệt chủng
existingExample: Poaching has pushed many endangered species to the edge of extinction.

definitionEn: gases sent into the air, especially from vehicles and factories.
existingExample: Stricter regulations are needed to curb emissions from heavy industry.

definitionEn: able to continue for a long time without damaging the environment.
existingExample: Sustainable farming protects the soil for future generations.

definitionEn: the process of something being damaged or made worse.
existingExample: Overgrazing has led to severe land degradation in some regions.

definitionEn: to make something harmful less severe.
existingExample: Planting trees in cities can help mitigate the effects of heatwaves.

definitionEn: a place where waste is buried under the ground.
existingExample: Most plastic packaging ends up in landfill or in the ocean.

definitionEn: plastic items designed to be thrown away after one use.
existingExample: Several countries have banned single-use plastics such as straws and bags.

definitionEn: the protection of the natural environment, plants and animals.
existingExample: Conservation efforts have helped some whale populations recover.

definitionEn: the natural home of an animal or plant.
existingExample: Habitat loss is one of the greatest threats to wildlife.

definitionEn: very severe weather such as floods, droughts or storms.
existingExample: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent as the climate warms.

definitionEn: a long period with little or no rain.
existingExample: A prolonged drought can devastate crops and drive up food prices.

definitionEn: impossible to change back to a previous state.
existingExample: Scientists warn that some damage to ecosystems may be irreversible.

definitionEn: to treat used materials so that they can be used again.
existingExample: Local councils should make it easier for residents to recycle household waste.

definitionEn: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other.
existingExample: Introducing a new species can disrupt a fragile ecosystem.

definitionEn: a substance that makes air, water or soil dirty or harmful.
existingExample: Factories must filter pollutants before releasing waste water into rivers.

definitionEn: the gradual increase in the temperature of the earth's atmosphere.
existingExample: Tackling global warming requires cooperation between all nations.

definitionEn: a tax on fuels based on how much carbon dioxide they produce.
existingExample: A carbon tax would encourage companies to adopt cleaner technologies.

definitionEn: a reduction in the amount of something until very little remains.
existingExample: Overfishing has led to the depletion of fish stocks in many seas.

definitionEn: not harmful to the environment.
existingExample: Consumers are increasingly willing to pay more for eco-friendly products.

definitionEn: to make more people know about a problem or issue.
existingExample: Social media campaigns can raise awareness of environmental issues among young people.

definitionEn: caused by human activity.
existingExample: Most scientists agree that recent warming is largely anthropogenic.

definitionEn: the warming of the earth caused by gases trapping heat in the atmosphere.
existingExample: Methane intensifies the greenhouse effect far more than carbon dioxide in the short term.

definitionEn: producing no net carbon emissions.
existingExample: The company aims to become carbon neutral by 2035.

definitionEn: a state in which emissions are balanced by removal from the atmosphere.
existingExample: Many countries have pledged to reach net zero by 2050.

definitionEn: to reduce the carbon emissions of an activity or sector.
existingExample: Electric trains help decarbonise transport.

definitionEn: to capture and store carbon so it does not enter the atmosphere.
existingExample: Peatlands sequester large amounts of carbon.

definitionEn: the impact of a person or community on the environment.
existingExample: Eating less meat can reduce your ecological footprint.

definitionEn: using natural resources faster than they can recover.
existingExample: Overexploitation has driven some fisheries to collapse.

definitionEn: catching so many fish that populations cannot recover.
existingExample: Overfishing threatens the livelihoods of coastal communities.

definitionEn: illegally hunting or catching animals.
existingExample: Rhino poaching is driven by demand for horn.

definitionEn: the death of an entire species.
existingExample: Many amphibians are on the brink of extinction.

definitionEn: a strip of habitat connecting separate natural areas.
meaningVi: hành lang động vật hoang dã
existingExample: Wildlife corridors allow animals to move safely between forests.

definitionEn: replanting trees where forest has been lost.
existingExample: Reforestation can restore damaged river catchments.

definitionEn: the process by which fertile land becomes desert.
existingExample: Overgrazing accelerates desertification.

definitionEn: the washing or blowing away of the top layer of soil.
existingExample: Tree roots help prevent soil erosion.

definitionEn: a lack of sufficient clean water.
existingExample: Population growth worsens water scarcity in dry regions.

definitionEn: the increase in the average level of the oceans.
existingExample: Low-lying deltas are threatened by sea-level rise.

definitionEn: a period of unusually hot weather.
existingExample: Prolonged heatwaves put elderly people at risk.

definitionEn: a sudden, severe flood.
existingExample: Heavy rain triggered flash floods in the mountains.

definitionEn: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties or damage.
meaningVi: khả năng chống chịu, phục hồi
existingExample: Mangroves increase the resilience of coastlines to storms.

definitionEn: changes made to cope with new conditions.
existingExample: Sea walls are one form of climate adaptation.

definitionEn: to make something impure by adding a harmful substance.
existingExample: Chemicals from farms can contaminate drinking water.

definitionEn: containing poisonous substances capable of causing serious harm or death.
existingExample: Illegal dumping of toxic waste harms local communities.

definitionEn: air pollution mixed with fog.
existingExample: Thick smog forced schools in the capital to close.

definitionEn: tiny particles in the air that damage health.
existingExample: High levels of particulate matter damage the lungs.

definitionEn: rain made acidic by air pollution.
existingExample: Acid rain damaged forests across Europe in the 1980s.

definitionEn: a layer of the atmosphere that blocks harmful ultraviolet rays.
existingExample: The ban on CFCs has helped the ozone layer recover.

definitionEn: able to break down naturally.
existingExample: Biodegradable packaging reduces plastic pollution.

definitionEn: that cannot be replaced once used up.
existingExample: Oil and coal are non-renewable resources.

definitionEn: producing electricity from moving water.
existingExample: Hydroelectric dams can displace local communities.

definitionEn: electricity produced by nuclear reactions.
existingExample: Nuclear power produces little carbon but creates radioactive waste.

definitionEn: using less energy to perform the same task.
existingExample: Better insulation improves the energy efficiency of homes.

definitionEn: protected land around a city where building is restricted.
existingExample: Building on the green belt is highly controversial.

definitionEn: areas of land covered by shallow water.
existingExample: Wetlands act as natural flood defences.

definitionEn: a tree that grows in coastal salt water.
existingExample: Mangrove forests protect coastlines from storms.
